s: A company wants to migrate its website from an on-premises data center onto AWS. At the same time, it wants to migrate the website to a containerized microservice-based architecture to improve the availability and cost efficiency. The company's security policy states that privileges and network permissions must be configured according to best practice, using least privilege. A Solutions Architect must create a containerized architecture that meets the security requirements and has deployed the application to an Amazon ECS cluster. What steps are required after the deployment to meet the requirements? (Choose two.)
o: Create tasks using the bridge network mode.
Create tasks using the awsvpc network mode.
Apply security groups to Amazon EC2 instances, and use IAM roles for EC2 instances to access other resources.
Apply security groups to the tasks, and pass IAM credentials into the container at launch time to access other resources.
Apply security groups to the tasks, and use IAM roles for tasks to access other resources.
e: The awsvpc network mode provides each task with its own elastic network interface (ENI) and a primary private IP address1. By using this network mode, the solutions architect can isolate the tasks from each other and apply security groups to the tasks directly2. This way, the solutions architect can control the inbound and outbound traffic at the task level and enforce the least privilege principle3. IAM roles for tasks allow the solutions architect to assign permissions to each task separately, so that they can access other AWS resources that they need4. By using IAM roles for tasks, the solutions architect can avoid passing IAM credentials into the container at launch time, which is less secure and more prone to errors5. awsvpc network mode Task networking with the awsvpc network mode Security groups for your VPC IAM roles for tasks Best practices for managing AWS access keys

w.y: "Least privilege" for both network and privileges decides it. awsvpc network mode gives each task its own ENI so security groups can be applied per task, and IAM roles for tasks give each task only the permissions it needs.

o.A: Bridge mode shares the host's network interface, so security groups cannot be applied per task.
o.B: Correct: awsvpc mode gives each task its own ENI and security group.
o.C: Instance-level security groups and roles give every container on the host the same access, not least privilege.
o.D: Passing long-term IAM credentials into containers is against best practice.
o.E: Correct: per-task security groups plus task IAM roles give least privilege for network and AWS access.
